props.title: Two for the Road
props.initialSlug: A couple's marriage unfolds across multiple road trips

sections.content: Two for the Road revolutionized nonlinear storytelling in romantic cinema. Director Stanley Donen and screenwriter Frederic Raphael crafted an innovative narrative that jumps between multiple timelines, following Audrey Hepburn and Albert Finney's marriage across 12 years and several road trips through France. This sophisticated approach influenced later relationship studies like Annie Hall (1977) and (500) Days of Summer (2009). The film's bold editing techniques and fragmented chronology were radical for 1967, predating similar experiments in Don't Look Now (1973) and Out of Sight (1998).

sections.content: The film's examination of how time affects romance created a template for modern relationship dramas. Like Blue Valentine (2010) and Marriage Story (2019), it fearlessly depicts both the euphoric beginnings and painful deterioration of a relationship. Hepburn and Finney's chemistry evolves convincingly across multiple time periods, showing both playful youth and worn-down middle age, anticipating similar temporal experiments in The Way We Were (1973).

Visually, Donen brought his musical background (Singin' in the Rain (1952)) to create fluid transitions between time periods. The innovative use of match cuts and location repetition to bridge different eras influenced directors like Nicolas Roeg and Steven Soderbergh. The film's sophisticated costume design by Paco Rabanne helps orient viewers in different time periods while reflecting the changing relationship dynamics. SUBHEAD: Style and Fashion Innovation

sections.content: The film serves as a remarkable time capsule of 1960s fashion evolution, with Hepburn's wardrobe by Ken Scott, Mary Quant, and Paco Rabanne tracking changing styles across the decade. Her looks influenced contemporary fashion and later period films like An Education (2009) and A Single Man (2009). The automotive progression through different Mercedes models similarly charts the passing years while maintaining the road movie aesthetic that influenced later European travelogues like Y Tu Mamá También (2001).
